items.statement:
Let a proper gadget family have encoding $V$, correction capacity $d$, and effective spread budget $\ell$ as in [[def-qc-ft-gadget-and-proper-code-contract]]. Fix $q\ge1$ with $2q\ell\le d$ and put $b=q\ell$. Assume type-compatible recursive replacement and the following additional **finite port-substitution hypothesis**, proved for the actual finite templates. It is not implied by their one-level encoded-input contracts alone.

In one substitution experiment replace each elementary port by any finite encoded port $U$ with a correctable error span $\mathcal T$ and an attached private syndrome register. Good replacements have their declared ideal logical channel/instrument tensored with syndrome maps on their admitted sectors. Intermediate computation-output and correction-input sectors must be specified; they are correctable, and complete corrected boundaries use $\mathcal T$. Marked replacements are arbitrary CPTP maps on their own physical ports, with possibly unencoded outputs. Correction and designated input refresh have noisy arbitrary-input attraction into their declared residual ranges, without a logical-preservation assertion on arbitrary inputs.

For the outer block let $\mathcal H_s(\mathcal T)$ be the span of tensor operators with at most $s$ unrestricted child factors and all other factors in $\mathcal T$, and let $\widetilde V=U^{\otimes m}V$; use the corresponding typed factors when port types differ. For at most $q$ marked replacements, the finite hypothesis requires computation to map $\mathcal H_b(\mathcal T)\widetilde V$ to $\mathcal H_{2b}(\mathcal T)\widetilde Vg$ and correction to map $\mathcal H_d(\mathcal T)\widetilde V$ to $\mathcal H_b(\mathcal T)\widetilde V$, preserving the specified ideal logical instrument. Correction and designated refresh must also attract arbitrary inputs into their stipulated residual ranges. These are joint, outcome-resolved Kraus-span identities, with arbitrary syndrome coefficients, full trace preservation on admitted domains, and identity on the external reference.

The finite proof must specify an acyclic order for these assertions, retaining any stronger zero-marked clause it uses. In particular it must show where an inadmissible port is refreshed before interaction, that this cleanup can be absorbed into its preceding marked map without enlarging that map's ports, and that still-inadmissible outputs lie in the residual support already counted. This is a hypothesis about one finite template with abstract ports, not correctness assumed at every concatenation level.

If each computation stage and its correction stage have at most $q$ bad child rectangles, then after correction at level $r\ge1$ the joint instrument has hierarchical residual sector $\mathcal E_{r;b}$, defined below, after its ideal logical target. The recursively decoded recovery $D_r$ returns that target exactly, including every finite external reference and recorded logical outcome. At level one this is the ordinary encoded-instrument relation; at higher levels it does not bound the total number of elementary physical errors by $d$.

items.title: An Explicit Proper Code and Universal Fault-Tolerant Gadgets
items.statement: There is an explicit fixed quantum code and finite logical gate set whose generated subgroup, including adjoints, is dense in the unitary group on its logical space in operator norm, and whose encoder, error-correction, initialization, readout, and gate gadgets satisfy the proper-code contract of [[def-qc-ft-gadget-and-proper-code-contract]]. A Steane $t=1$ construction must be paired with a separately proved extended-rectangle correctness and overlap analysis. A route using the concatenated threshold theorem with $d\ge2\ell$ must exhibit a code correcting at least $2\ell$ located errors and prove every required gadget contract.

items.title: Concatenated Threshold Under Local-Stochastic Correlated Noise
items.statement:
Assume a fixed proper code of block size $m\ge2d+1$ and correction capacity $d\ge1$, with a recursively closed finite gadget family satisfying [[def-qc-ft-gadget-and-proper-code-contract]]. Let its positive integer effective spread budget be $\ell$, let $a\ge2$ bound the number of child rectangles, put $q=\lfloor d/(2\ell)\rfloor$, and assume $1\le q<a$. Assume also the proved finite port-substitution hypothesis of [[lem-qc-sparse-fault-path-implies-code-deviation]] for these parameters, including its noisy attraction and intermediate-sector requirements, and use its recursive final decoder. Put $A=\binom a{q+1}$. At each integer level $r\ge0$, use the full-depth recursive rectangle hierarchy: every root-to-location path has exactly $r$ child edges, and sibling location sets are disjoint. Use the finite channel-location schedule of [[def-qc-finite-channel-location-schedule]] and local-stochastic fault model of [[def-qc-local-stochastic-noise-model]], with $\eta\in[0,1]$ and $A\eta^q<1$. For each finite simulated circuit, let $N\ge1$ be its total number of top-level rectangles, counting every gate, initialization, correction, scheduled idle, measurement, and readout gadget. Then the level-$r$ bad-rectangle bound is
$$
p_r\le A^{-1/q}\bigl(A^{1/q}\eta\bigr)^{(q+1)^r}.
$$
The noisy computation starts at an admitted encoded boundary: pre-existing live data blocks are jointly encoded from an arbitrary logical input, with any finite external reference retained, and any newly initialized blocks are supplied by the protected prescribed-initialization gadgets covered by the contract and counted among the top-level rectangles. No guarantee is asserted for an unknown unencoded physical input before this protection begins.
The probability that any of the $N$ top-level rectangles is bad, decoded-output trace distance, finite-POVM total-variation error, and success-probability change are each at most $Np_r$. For any target $0<\delta\le1$, choose the least $r$ such that $N A^{-1/q}(A^{1/q}\eta)^{(q+1)^r}\le\delta$ (for $\eta=0$, take $r=0$). For fixed code and gadget parameters, as $N/\delta\to\infty$, this gives $O(\log\log(N/\delta))$ concatenation levels and polylogarithmic fixed-code overhead. Fault indicators need not be independent; conditional operations remain local to their specified locations.

items.title: Conditional Concatenated Threshold for Proper Codes
items.statement:
Assume a fixed proper code with integer block size $m\ge2d+1$, integer correction capacity $d\ge1$, positive integer effective spread budget $\ell$, and an integer bound $a\ge2$ on the number of child rectangles per gadget. Let $q=\lfloor d/(2\ell)\rfloor$ and assume $1\le q<a$. Assume also the proved finite port-substitution hypothesis of [[lem-qc-sparse-fault-path-implies-code-deviation]] for these parameters, including its noisy attraction and intermediate-sector requirements. Put $A=\binom{a}{q+1}$. At each integer level $r\ge0$, use the full-depth recursive rectangle hierarchy: every root-to-location path has exactly $r$ child edges, and sibling location sets are disjoint. Use the independent local CPTP fault model of [[def-qc-noise-channel-model]] with rate $\eta\in[0,1]$, and assume $A\eta^q<1$. The circuit is a finite channel-location schedule as in [[def-qc-finite-channel-location-schedule]]. Interpret level-$r$ outputs after the recursive decoded recovery $D_r$ of [[lem-qc-sparse-fault-path-implies-code-deviation]], built from the declared one-level recovery. For each finite simulated circuit, let $N\ge1$ be its total number of top-level rectangles, counting every gate, initialization, correction, scheduled idle, measurement, and readout gadget. Then every level-$r$ rectangle is bad with probability at most
$$
p_r\le A^{-1/q}\bigl(A^{1/q}\eta\bigr)^{(q+1)^r}.
$$
The noisy computation starts at an admitted encoded boundary: pre-existing live data blocks are jointly encoded from an arbitrary logical input, with any finite external reference retained, and any newly initialized blocks are supplied by the protected prescribed-initialization gadgets covered by the contract and counted among the top-level rectangles. No guarantee is asserted for an unknown unencoded physical input before this protection begins. The probability that any of the $N$ top-level rectangles is bad is at most $Np_r$. For every admitted jointly encoded logical input, including one entangled with an arbitrary finite reference, the decoded level-$r$ output has trace distance at most $Np_r$ from the ideal logical output; every final finite POVM output law has total-variation distance at most $Np_r$, so every success probability changes by at most $Np_r$. For any target $0<\delta\le1$, choose the least $r$ such that $N A^{-1/q}(A^{1/q}\eta)^{(q+1)^r}\le\delta$ (for $\eta=0$, take $r=0$). For fixed code and gadget parameters, as $N/\delta\to\infty$, this level is $O(\log\log(N/\delta))$, and the fixed-code size and depth overhead are polylogarithmic in $N/\delta$. This conditional theorem does not supply a concrete universal gadget family; that is a separate authoring obligation.
